title: Engineering Signals of Human-AI Collaboration in the Agentic Coding Era: A Longitudinal Analysis of 33,228 Pull Requests from vLLM and SGLang with Implications for Biomedical AI Agents and Bioinformatics Pipeline Developmen
abstract: arXiv:2608.13884v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The rapid adoption of AI coding assistants and autonomous agentic development systems has coincided with major changes in the pace and structure of open-source software engineering. Yet empirical longitudinal evidence of these changes at the team level remains limited. We present a descriptive longitudinal analysis of seven engineering metrics: pull request (PR) throughput, cycle time, contributor diversity, PR comment density, merge rate, new-author participation, and PR size. Metrics were computed from all merged PRs in two high-velocity AI infrastructure repositories, vLLM (February 2023-June 2026; 18,290 PRs) and SGLang (January 2024-June 2026; 14,938 PRs). We segment development into four eras aligned with major changes in AI-assisted software development and examine human- and bot-authored activities. Both projects show substantial increases in development velocity and AI-developer collaboration signals. PR throughput increased 2

translated_title: 人机协作在智能体编码时代中的工程信号：来自vLLM和SGLang的33,228个拉取请求的纵向分析及其对生物医学AI智能体和生物信息学流水线开发的启示
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13884v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：AI编码助手和自主智能体开发系统的快速普及，与开源软件工程速度和结构的重大变化相伴随。然而，团队层面上这些变化的经验性纵向证据仍然有限。我们提出了对七项工程指标的描述性纵向分析：拉取请求（PR）吞吐量、周期时间、贡献者多样性、PR评论密度、合并率、新作者参与度和PR规模。这些指标是从两个高速度AI基础设施仓库中所有已合并的PR计算得出的，分别是vLLM（2023年2月至2026年6月；18,290个PR）和SGLang（2024年1月至2026年6月；14,938个PR）。我们将开发过程划分为四个与AI辅助软件开发重大变化相对应的时代，并检查了人类和机器人作者的活动。两个项目都显示出开发速度和AI开发者协作信号的显著增长。PR吞吐量增加了2倍。
tldr: 通过对vLLM和SGLang两个AI基础设施仓库的33,228个拉取请求进行纵向分析，本研究揭示了AI编码时代中团队开发速度和协作信号的显著变化，为生物医学AI智能体应用提供了实证参考。
en_tdlr: A longitudinal analysis of 33,228 pull requests from vLLM and SGLang reveals significant increases in development velocity and AI-developer collaboration signals during the agentic coding era, offering empirical insights for biomedical AI agents.
